newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs slip on caution ahead tankan.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs slip on caution ahead tankan.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen and Japanese government bond (JGB) futures were lower late on Thursday as players turned cautious ahead of next week's tankan and Japanese bond auctions.

Dealers said both ends of the Japanese yield curve opened firm on overnight news Japan's Ministry of Finance had ordered the liquidation of Hanwa Bank, a second-tier regional bank, due to its bad debts.

But the market failed to sustain its gains as players largely shrugged off the news. "For the Japanese, it was no news. It's a small bank and the market already knew about it," said a trader with a Japanese futures house.
He said JGBs were unlikely to gain much ground ahead of the Bank of Japan's quarterly tankan survey of business sentiment and the Finance Ministry's bond auctions next week.
He said the 2.7 percent coupon on the 10-year bond auction was unlikely to draw much interest.
December JGBs ended at 124.44 against their opening 124.72. June Euroyen stood at 99.22 at 1120 GMT against its IMM close at 99.24, which was also its high for the day.
A dealer with another Japanese institution said the December JGB contract showed potential to fall below 124.00 to cover a gap on the charts.
But he added that players were unlikely to sell the contract aggressively ahead of its rollover.
"The short end of the curve is not so volatile. Even with the Hanwa news, it only rose three or four ticks before coming off again," he said, adding that June Euroyen would be supported at 99.17.

Eurodollar futures remained lethargic on a dearth of leads. March and June each ended one tick below their IMM closes at 94.51 and 94.44 respectively. Turnover for both months was less than 7,000 lots.
"The trend is definitely on the buy side. People who are short are waiting for it to go back down so they can come back in," said the trader with the first institution.
